problemStatement.formal:
Can every integer $N\geq 2$ be written as\[N=\frac{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(m+i)}{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(n+i)}\]for some $k\geq 2$ and $m\geq n+k$?



If $n$ and $k$ are fixed then can one say anything about the set of integers so represented?

See also [677].

insights: representable_set_infinite proved: for fixed n,k, choosing m=n+t*P(n,k) gives infinitely many integer ratios
Key insight: (n+i)|P(n,k) for each factor, so shifting by multiples of P(n,k) preserves divisibility
consecutiveProduct is strictly monotone, so the quotient function is injective (distinct t give distinct values)
